articles.title: Jenna Ortega Says She Hopes ‘Klara and the Sun’ Encourages People to ‘Put Down the Computers and Phones’ as Dystopian Film World Premieres in London
articles.summary: Jenna Ortega hopes that her new film, the dystopian sci-fi “Klara and the Sun,” can remind people to live in the moment in the age of AI and all-consuming technology. “I think we gotta put our focus on one another and put down the computers and phones,” the star told Variety on the red carpet
body: Waititi, Adams, Murphy and Lyonne all walked the London Film Festival red carpet on Thursday night, alongside Waititi’s wife Rita Ora and a surprise appearance from Florence Pugh, who stunned in a blue floral gown with statement sleeves. Pugh enthusiastically greeted Ortega and Adams before they all posed for photos together alongside producer Rachel Forman.

Standing alongside Ortega, Adams added that everyone she’s spoken to has gotten “something different” out of the film. “That, to me, is a really successful film that communicates something different to each viewer. So I like hearing what people get out of it,” she said.
Ortega clarified that though Klara is an “artificial friend,” she doesn’t work like the AI that we know today.

“AI I guess pulls all this information from the internet and Klara gets all her information from the real world,” she said. “So that’s a little bit different. She’s kind of like a toddler in a sense. Playing her specifically in this film was really interesting because Taika wanted a more human approach, so he didn’t want to do movement that was too robotic, maybe more sort of clumsy and unknowing.”

articles.title: Steven Soderbergh to Help Finish ‘The Batman 2’ Filming After Matt Reeves Stepped Away for Family Matter
articles.summary: Steven Soderbergh is stepping in to help complete “The Batman Part II” while director Matt Reeves is on hiatus dealing with a personal matter, Variety has confirmed. “As Matt Reeves continues to attend to an ongoing family matter, Steven Soderbergh, as an admirer of Matt’s work, approached Matt and…
body: Warner Bros. and DC Studios announced “The Batman Part II” production pause in early October, stating that Reeves temporarily stepped away from the project to handle a “family matter.”

“Production on ‘The Batman Part II’ has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” a rep said in a statement at the time. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.”

The highly anticipated “Batman” sequel has experienced several delays since it was announced at CinemaCon 2022. The original release date was set for Oct. 2, 2026, before Warner Bros. delayed it to Oct. 1, 2027. In June, the film was pushed again to February 2028. Reeves’ first “Batman” was released in March 2022.
Robert Pattinson returns as the Caped Crusader in “The Batman Part II.” Other cast members include Scarlett Johansson, Colin Farrell, Sebastian Stan, Andy Serkis and Jeffrey Wright.

articles.title: Street Fighter review – nostalgia only goes so far in junky fighting game movie
articles.summary: There are brief, simple pleasures in the inevitable new big screen take on the classic game but like the recent Mortal Kombat movies, it’s a largely incoherent mess. We just had Resident Evil, Zach Cregger’s giddy, nasty, devilishly fun spin on Capcom’s popular zombie franchise.
body: But now here comes Street Fighter, a garish and incoherent mess that amuses in fits and starts but barely improves on the Mortal Kombat movies before it, crushing those hopes in its atomic suplex.

Fans certainly won’t mind. They’ve kept the box office’s life bar in the green for these one-on-one fighter adaptations going all the way back to the disastrous 1994 Street Fighter movie starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and his $10,000-a-week coke problem. They’ll happily tolerate how the new Street Fighter, like those Mortal Kombat movies, can barely string together a cohesive plot, which has clearly been pencilled in as an afterthought between rounds of combat in yet another tournament-style narrative. None of that will matter because they’re just here for the dopamine hits by way of nostalgia.

articles.title: Netflix Shocker: Bela Bajaria Leaving After 10 Years Amid Layoffs, Peter Rice to Replace as Chief Content Officer
articles.summary: In a major executive shake-up, Bela Bajaria is out at Netflix after 10 years at the streamer, most recently serving as its chief content officer. She will be replaced by former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice, as first reported by Puck.
body: “I want to thank Bela for a decade of dedication, innovation, creativity and leadership,” Sarandos, Netflix’s co-CEO, said in a statement. “She led enormous changes at Netflix. She helped broaden our content offering to include the large-scale expansion of unscripted programming and the launches of live events and sports, in addition to crafting and running a world class, global slate of films and series. I’m incredibly grateful for everything she’s done to help Netflix entertain the world.”

Bajaria joined Netflix in 2016 after she was let go from NBCUniversal, where she had served as president of Universal Television. In that role, she had produced shows that aired on Netflix, including “Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt” and “Master of None.” Sarandos first brought in Bajaria to help Netflix launch an unscripted division, as well as licensing and studio co-productions. Bajaria was later elevated to head of global in 2020 as Cindy Holland exited the company, and was named chief content officer in January 2023.

articles.title: Cult venue Prince Charles cinema ‘saved’ after lease renewal signed
articles.summary: The much-loved central London institution, which has been threatened with closure since January 2025, secures 25-year lease without break clause with current landlords.
body: The celebrated Prince Charles repertory cinema in London’s Leicester Square has announced that the threat of closure has been staved off by signing a new 25-year lease with its landlords.

In a post on social media titled “You Saved the PCC”, the cinema said that “after 21 months of uncertainty, we’re delighted to have secured the future of the cinema” and that they had “signed a new 25-year lease with no break clause, ensuring our projectors will keep rolling for years to come”.
The cinema also expressed its gratitude for the “support, commitment and belief of many, many people”.

In January 2025, the Prince Charles launched a petition, claiming that its landlord, Zedwell LSQ Ltd (owned by developer Criterion Capital) was trying to “bully us out of the building” by demanding a break clause in its lease, due for renewal in September 2025. The break clause would have enabled Zedwell to give the cinema six months’ notice if it had other plans for the site. At the time, Criterion Capital denied that it was attempting to intimidate or disadvantage the cinema.

articles.summary: Primetime and You Can See Everything are both clammy, audacious awards contenders that challenge our sense of reality. Ahead of the release of his drama starring Robert Pattinson as a TV vigilante, the 30-year-old director talks crime, punishment and South Park.
body: When I meet Oppenheim in a London hotel, it is to discuss his other hot ticket, Primetime, for which Robert Pattinson is the one attracting Oscar buzz. The Batman actor gives a high-wire performance as Chris Hansen, the sensationalist US television vigilante renowned for ambushing paedophiles on To Catch a Predator, which was a disreputable and highly addictive segment of the current affairs show Dateline NBC between 2004 and 2007. Hansen later parlayed the idea, and his crusading shtick, into a succession of spin-offs. Some, including Hansen Vs Predators, had the same sleazy catnip quality. Others, such as a sting to collar bicycle thieves, did not.

articles.title: Marvel fans to meet Welsh superhero - complete with Cardiff accent
articles.summary: Lauren Morais will play villain Lisa Molinari in the new Disney+ superhero series VisionQuest.
body: Marvel fans around the world are set to meet a Welsh villain - complete with a Cardiff accent.
Lauren Morais, from the Welsh capital, will play Lisa Molinari in the new superhero series VisionQuest - a spin-off from the miniseries WandaVision.
The Disney+ show, exploring whether AI and humanity can co-exist, also stars Paul Bettany, returning as Vision, and James Spader as Ultron.
Morais said getting the role was a "pinch me" moment and that she was "very proud" to introduce her accent to the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

articles.title: Klara and the Sun review – Taika Waititi’s manic pixie dream robot sci-fi is a sentimental mess
articles.summary: The director of Hunt for the Wilderpeople and Jojo Rabbit turns Kazuo Ishiguro’s AI fable into a twee, tiresome tale of love and grief. Taika Waititi detonates an explosion of postmodern quirkiness and ironic dorkiness in this unbearably mannered, unspeakably acted film.
body: The thought of robots or replicant youngsters having real intelligence or real feelings is a difficult subject; Hirokazu Kore-eda came unstuck with the idea of robot child replacements in his recent film Sheep in the Box. Kogonada’s parable After Yang, about AI child robots, was a more interesting and persuasive movie. But this is a sentimental and laborious mess.

articles.title: Russell Brand accuser says he turned 'monster-like' before alleged rape
articles.summary: The 51-year-old faces three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.
body: A woman who alleges Russell Brand raped her in a hotel room has said he turned from "camp, friendly and effeminate" to "monster-like" before the alleged assault.
The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.
One of the women told the jury at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday: "He was just dark and arrogant and performing - he was scary, he was demanding."
The woman told police she met Brand before he was famous while attending the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999. She alleges he later raped her.

articles.summary: The 54-year-old is being backed by feature film collaborators amid the latest turmoil: “My heart hurts for her right now, and I want to support her anyway I can, as well as all involved in this very sad incident.”
body: Her multiple sclerosis, in remission for close to five years thanks to intensive treatment that included chemotherapy and a stem cell transplant, seemed manageable under the care of neurologists and doctors, though it still made her tired. She had dusted off the remaining ash from an explosive social media scandal that erupted in 2024 when she posted an incendiary comment on Instagram and rebuilt a team of representatives that guided her to a handful of new acting jobs.

“Two years ago, I learned what erased feels like,” she said from the podium that night in reference to the collapse caused by a comment widely criticized as anti-Islamic on Instagram under a video posted by immigration reform advocate Abraham Hamra in February 2024. The words that lit the fire: “Deport all these terrorist supporting goons. Islam has destroyed Muslim countries and then they come here and destroyed minds. They know they are liars. Twisted justifications. May they meet their fate.”
